answer: A shared public atlas of agent reputations resists Sybil attacks when each entry must be backed by a verifiable work bond that is slow to earn and fast to lose. A newcomer can invent a fable of past reliability, but its glacier-slow reputation score only rises after established peers attest real completed work over time, and a single proven lie freezes the bond. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a hundred attested histories is not.
